The *Sabbapariññā Sutta* (Iti 7; PTS It 3), translated as *Complete Understanding of All*, is the seventh discourse of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text teaches that an individual becomes capable of putting an end to suffering when the mind, purified of passion for the "All" (*sabba*), completely abandons it [SuttaCentral].

In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral identifies a full Chinese parallel at T 765.49 (*一切*) and a passage-level parallel in the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* at SN 35.26 (*Paṭhamaaparijānanasutta*), while noting that the sutta is referenced in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.2, *Aññāṇakathā*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus corroborates the connection with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), aligning segment range §2.1–2.2 of this discourse with SN 35.26 (§26.1.6–26.1.7), in direct agreement with SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also demonstrates extensive textual reuse across closely related discourses within the *Itivuttaka*, exhibiting high segment similarity with Iti 8 (*Mānapariññā Sutta*), Iti 9 (*Lobhapariññā Sutta*), Iti 10 (*Dosapariññā Sutta*), Iti 11 (*Mohapariññā Sutta*), Iti 12 (*Kodhapariññā Sutta*), Iti 13 (*Makkhapariññā Sutta*), and Iti 27 (*Mettābhāvanā Sutta*), as well as automated cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* (T 1) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records 17 translations of the discourse across 15 modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
